title: Breaking Memory Bottlenecks in Quantum Control Systems for More Precise Experiments and Higher Throughput Computing
authors: Yicheng Guang, Neel Vora, Yilun Xu, Yueqi Chen, Gang Huang
abstract: As quantum computing continues to demonstrate promise and attract growing attention, there is an increasing need for more precise experiments to advance the development of quantum devices, as well as higher circuit throughput to validate more domain applications. However, this need is hindered by a memory bottleneck at the quantum control system layer, arising from limited on-chip BRAM capacity and the non-deterministic latency of DRAM. To break this bottleneck, we present Ant-Q, a memory hierarchy design that integrates DRAM with BRAM to support pipelined quantum circuit execution while ensuring deterministic inter-circuit timing. We evaluated Ant-Q using 26 real-world experimental and computing circuits. The results show that Ant-Q supports deep circuits for 1Q and 2Q Randomized Benchmarking and reduces the overhead of circuit loading and readout uplink relative to execution time from 22.90%-1417.05% to near zero. Ant-Q is being integrated into QubiC 3.0, with part of its functionalities already available.
summary: The paper introduces Ant-Q, a novel memory hierarchy designed for quantum control systems to overcome severe bottlenecks caused by limited on-chip memory and slow data transfer. By implementing a pipelined workflow that overlaps circuit loading with execution, Ant-Q significantly boosts system throughput and allows for the running of much deeper and more complex quantum experiments.
main_problem: The development of precise quantum experiments and high-throughput quantum computation is limited by a memory bottleneck within the classical quantum control system layer.
main_result: The proposed Ant-Q memory hierarchy design successfully transforms the inefficient 'punched-card' workflow into a pipelined architecture, reducing I/O overhead to near zero and enabling deep circuit execution.
method: Ant-Q integrates DRAM with BRAM on the control board to create a pipeline that overlaps data loading, quantum circuit execution, and result readout, bypassing sequential bottlenecks.
model_or_system: The work focuses on optimizing FPGA-based quantum control systems (like QubiC 3.0) which interface classical processing units with Quantum Processing Units (QPUs). The system architecture involves managing data flow between DRAM (large capacity) and BRAM (fast cache) on the Programmable Logic.
key_observables: Overhead reduction percentage relative to execution time, support for deep Randomized Benchmarking circuits, and overall batch throughput improvement.
important_parameters: BRAM capacity limits ($\le 2048$ commands), DRAM non-deterministic latency (refresh cycles), and the comparison between old vs. new system overheads.
main_assumptions: The primary bottleneck is memory structure; future work plans include bypassing the PS-to-host link and implementing predictive preloading for cross-buffer jumps.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the transformation from a sequential 'Punched-Card workflow' to an overlapped, pipelined workflow in Ant-Q, detailing data paths and buffer usage.
paper_structure: The paper identifies the memory bottleneck, proposes the Ant-Q memory hierarchy integrating DRAM/BRAM for pipelining, evaluates its performance using real-world circuits (RB), quantifies overhead reduction, and discusses future scaling limitations.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses the classical control layer required to run complex quantum algorithms, which is crucial context for any theoretical physicist designing or simulating quantum hardware experiments.
